label: prose:mba-chain-map
title: From propositions to compute — the chain map
html:
Chain map. The following table outlines the eleven canonical steps of the substrate-to-observable chain, their justifying propositions, and Python entry points. Detailed per-step algorithm blocks follow.

# Step Required propositions Python API entry point Witness JSON Status
1 Categorical action \rho_n\colon B_n \to \mathrm{Aut}_{\mathbf{C}}(V^{\otimes n}) categorical-action of the braid group tools/hecke-engine/src/lib.rs (Rust crate) — proved
2 Non-abelian Stokes \to Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 = (q-q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1 Hecke relation; GS-rewriter confluence pyhecke.build_nucleon_nf / pyhecke.build_atom_nf (Rust core via pyhecke-native) hecke-core-symbolic-migration.witness.json proved
3 Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M on H_n(q) Alexander–Markov; uniqueness of \mathrm{tr}_M qou_mass.compute_tr_M(Z, N) / pyhecke.nf_tr(nf) markov-free-energy-qvalues.witness.json derived
4 Bring \chi = -6 brane (settled — Bring surface) script computations/bring_chiral_fibre_figure.py; constants in qou_substrate.constants bring-chiral-fibre-figure.witness.json derived
5 Wedderburn decomposition \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda\,\chi^\lambda Wedderburn / Wenzl decomposition pyhecke.wedderburn_weight(λ, q) + pyhecke.partitions_of(n) wedderburn-lp-ew-wiring.witness.json derived
6 Frobenius pairing \langle a,b\rangle_F + self-duality \Psi = S^2 = \mathrm{id} Frobenius pairing; self-duality pyhecke.check_frobenius(x) (script: audit_frobenius_pairing.py) — proved
7 Gröbner–Shirshov filtration / E_2 collapse GB spectral sequence script computations/gb_filtration_jet_tracker.py gb-filtration-jet-order.witness.json derived
8 Jet-prefix transport (q \to 1 limit) jet-order proposition script computations/gb_filtration_jet_order_reader.py gb-filtration-jet-order-reader.witness.json conditional
9a Nucleon mass ratio m_{\mathfrak{p}}/m_e via the muon-anchored Hecke energy m_{\mathfrak{p}} = 2\,(m_\mu F_{\mathrm{Bor}} - 6 m_e)\cdot R_{\mathrm{s5bb}} muon anchor m_\mu = m_e\,\mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2; Borromean dressing F_{\mathrm{Bor}} qou_mass.predict(atom) per-observable-100x-status.witness.json conditional
9b Per-isotope binding B(K) = m_e \cdot \sum_\lambda y_\lambda\,\chi^\lambda\,\Delta_\lambda binding-energy density (\Delta_\lambda open) qou_mass.predict(atom, observable="binding_energy") canonical-mass-table-242ppb.witness.json open
10 Confinement SDP and canonical T_w operator-selection LP; LP–SDP duality script computations/confinement-operator-selection.py (Python solver shim: pyhecke.lp_dual_solver) confinement-operator-selection.witness.json derived
11 \beta-decay \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = Q_{\mathrm{base}} \cdot \prod_k (1 + c_k\,u^k) \mathfrak{Q}_\beta derivation; c_k truncation order script computations/q_beta_predicted.py (CAL-3 pin: build_cal_3_q_beta_witness.py) cal-3-q-beta.witness.json (CAL-3 pin), q-beta-predicted.witness.json (predictions) derived

Sidecar algorithms. Four standalone algorithms support the production pipeline:

  1. \Delta_\lambda closure ansätze. The per-partition density at each isotope; currently open.
  2. c_k truncation ladder. The convergent series whose truncation order N is fixed by precision N \geq \lceil \log_{10}(1/\varepsilon) / 2.07 \rceil - 1.
  3. LP/SDP dual emission contract. Every operator-selection compute must emit primal and dual variables, enforced by lp_dual_witness_validator.py.
  4. Witness-JSON pipeline. Cross-language interchange schema and the WitnessBuilder pattern.
  5. Atomic electron layer (Level 6). M_{\mathrm{atom}} = M_{\mathrm{nuclear}} + Z\,m_e - B_{\mathrm{el}}(Z) with B_{\mathrm{el}} the bare-Z hydrogenic shell sum at the canonical e-Hartree scale E_h = \alpha_{EM}^2 m_e c^2 (CS-corrected \alpha_{EM} at arbitrary precision). Producer computations/atom_electron_mass.py, witness atom-electron-mass.witness.json; consumed by the mass dashboard's atomic table (derived B_{\mathrm{el}} since 2026-08-30, replacing the AME empirical fit, which is retained as a comparison). Inter-electron screening (Z_{\mathrm{eff}}) is open.

Location of the algorithm statements. The per-step blocks provide the precise input/output contract, correctness conditions, complexity estimate, and Python signature. These specifications alone suffice to reproduce every numerical prediction without referencing implementation source code.
